title: Cane Tejada Bodied Noma in Explosive Power Book II: Ghost Series Finale
htmlContent:
Power Book II: Ghost delivered a stunning season 4 finale, with Cane Tejada, one of its most ruthless characters, demonstrating his continuing strength. In episode ten, Cane faced the menacing drug lord, Noma Asaju, in a move that left fans stunned and craving more.

The Tejada family has had Cane Tejada, played by Woody McClain, as the unpredictable, fiercely loyal, and always-up-for-a-fight wildcard. His survival instincts were tested in the season finale when Noma, the deadly Queenpin, canceled Christmas on his mother, Monet Tejada. As a protective and power-hungry son, Cane couldn't let that slip.

After Noma killed Monet, Cane boldly decided to take her out, fully aware of the consequences. Cane shot Noma in the head during a tense scene that left viewers holding their breath, marking a significant turning point in the series. Noma's reign of terror, which had loomed over much of the season, ended abruptly, but Cane didn't get away unscathed.

As the police closed in on Cane following the murder, the episode became a non-stop barrage of shootouts. Cane, always ahead of the game, escaped multiple shootouts with the authorities but suffered injuries in the process. The character's resilience and determination were emphasized in the action-packed scenes, but it was evident that he was approaching his limit as he battled to survive.

The chaos left Cane bloodied and battered, barely able to stand. Effie Morales came to his aid, demonstrating once again that loyalty and betrayal can be equally dangerous in the Power Universe. Throughout the series, Effie has been navigating her dangerous path, and she gives Cane the money he requires to skip town.
